import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm


def plot_histograms(arrays: list) -> plt.Figure:
    """
    For each 2D numpy array in `arrays`, plot a histogram of the normalized
    (mean 0, std 1) data alongside the PDF of a standard normal distribution.

    Each array gets its own subplot in a single figure. Histograms are
    density-based, semi-transparent (alpha=0.6) and green; the PDF is overlaid
    in red with line width 2 over the range covering 99% of the standard
    normal distribution. Subplot titles indicate the index of the array.

    Parameters:
    - arrays: A list of 2D numpy arrays containing numerical data.

    Returns:
    - The matplotlib Figure containing all subplots.
    """
    n = len(arrays)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n, 1, squeeze=False)
    axes = axes.ravel()

    for i, (arr, ax) in enumerate(zip(arrays, axes)):
        data = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float).ravel()
        mean = np.mean(data)
        std = np.std(data)
        if std == 0:
            normalized_data = np.zeros_like(data)
        else:
            normalized_data = (data - mean) / std

        # Density-based, semi-transparent green histogram
        ax.hist(normalized_data, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='green')

        # Standard normal PDF covering 99% of the distribution
        x = np.linspace(norm.ppf(0.005), norm.ppf(0.995), 100)
        ax.plot(x, norm.pdf(x), 'r-', lw=2)

        ax.set_title(f'Array {i}')

    fig.suptitle('Histograms of Normalized Data with Standard Normal PDFs')
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig
